title: MSMT Report Says DPRK Overseas Labor Program Earned $450M–$800M in 2025 in Sanctions Breach; Pyongyang Rejects Findings
detail: The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) — a mechanism formed in October 2024 by the US, South Korea, Japan and other partners after China and Russia vetoed renewal of the UN Panel of Experts — issued a report on September 16, 2026 documenting continued DPRK deployment of overseas laborers in breach of UN Security Council resolutions banning the practice. The report found an estimated 35,600–101,280 North Korean workers active in at least 17 countries, primarily China and Russia, generating $450 million–$800 million in 2025 to help fund North Korea's nuclear weapons and ballistic missile programs. It said the DPRK state confiscates 80–90% of workers' wages, in some cases leaving laborers net indebted to the regime. North Korea's Foreign Ministry rejected the findings via KCNA, saying it would 'not tolerate' what it called hostile forces' efforts to curb its international cooperation, and characterized the overseas labor arrangements as 'normal, mutually beneficial economic cooperation' rather than sanctions violations, adding that no new sanctions would block its development or defense of its 'core interests.'

title: DPRK Defense Ministry Warns US-South Korea WMD Committee Talks Could Trigger Nuclear Force Law
detail: A spokesman for North Korea's Ministry of National Defence warned via KCNA on September 16, 2026 that the US-South Korea Counter-WMD Committee meeting — held September 10 at Seoul's Defense Ministry to strengthen information-sharing and joint response capabilities against DPRK weapons of mass destruction — 'could be regarded as a grave security challenge that calls for invoking' North Korea's 2022 state nuclear force policy law, which authorizes preemptive nuclear use in defined circumstances including a threat to the country's leadership or command-and-control system. The spokesman characterized the allied dialogue as a 'blatant declaration of confrontation' that treats using nuclear weapons against the North as predetermined strategy, and accused Washington and Seoul of using WMD accusations as cover for their own weapons development.
